Rashi on Ketubot 13a:10:1.hebrew: [ראוה מדברת - בפנויה, ומשום חששא דפסולין — לנתין ולממזר. וכיון שנבעלה לפסול, פסלה מן הכהונה]:
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:10:1.english: [They saw her speaking - [This refers to] an unmarried woman, and [the issue is] due to the concern of disqualified [men] — a natin or a mamzer. And once she has engaged in intercourse with a disqualified [man], he has disqualified her from the priesthood.]

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:10:2.hebrew: נאמנת - וכשרה לכהונה, ולא מספקינן לה בנבעלה לפסול לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:10:2.english: She is deemed credible - and [she is] fit for the priesthood, and we do not suspect her of having engaged in intercourse with one who is unfit for her.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:11:1.hebrew: היתה מעוברת כו' - בגמ' מפרש תרתי למה לי:
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:11:1.english: [If] she was pregnant, etc. - In the Gemara, it explains why two [cases] are needed.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:12:1.hebrew: נסתרה - ואע"פ שלא ראוה שנבעלה, נפסלה לכהונה לרבי יהושע כדלקמן, דמעלה עשו ביוחסין:
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:12:1.english: She secluded herself - And even though they did not see her engage in intercourse, she is disqualified from [marrying into] the priesthood according to Rabbi Yehoshua, as [stated] below, because they instituted a stringency regarding lineage.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:12:2.english: She eats and wipes her mouth - Thus, [the verse] uses the language of eating for intercourse.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:13:1.hebrew: בשלמא לזעירי היינו דקתני תרתי - מדברת — להודיעך כחו דר' יהושע, דאע"ג דלא ראוה שנבעלה, פסולה; ומעוברת — להודיעך כחו דרבן גמליאל:
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:13:1.english: Granted, according to Ze'eiri, that is [the reason] that [the Tanna] teaches two [cases] - "Speaking" [is taught] to inform you of the strength [of the position] of Rabbi Yehoshua, that even though they did not see her engage in intercourse, she is disqualified [from marrying a priest]; and "pregnant" [is taught] to inform you of the strength [of the position] of Rabban Gamliel.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:14:1.hebrew: בבתה - אם העובר הזה נקבה, תנשא לכהונה לר"ג. דאי אשמועינן בדידה, הוה אמינא: איהי, הואיל דהוה לה חזקה דכשרות מעיקרא, אמרי' אוקמה אחזקה ואל תפסילנה מספק; אבל עובר, דלא הוה ליה חזקה דכשרות, אימא לא:
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:14:1.english: Her daughter - If this fetus is female, she may marry into the priesthood according to Rabban Gamliel. For if [the Mishnah] had taught us [this] regarding [the mother] herself, I would have said: [as for] her, since she originally had a presumptive status of fitness, we say, "Establish her on her presumptive status and do not disqualify her out of doubt"; however, [regarding] a fetus, which did not have a presumptive status of fitness, I would say no.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:15:1.hebrew: הניחא למ"ד כו' - לקמן בשמעתין:
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:15:1.english: This works out well according to the one who says, etc. - [This is discussed] later in our sugya.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:15:2.hebrew: מאי איכא למימר - תרתי להכשיר בה למה לי, כיון דמדברת בראוה שנבעלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:15:2.english: What is there to say - Why do I need two [cases] to deem her fit, since [the case of] "speaking" [is one] where they saw that she had intercourse?

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:16:1.english: One flogs for seclusion - [With] lashes for rebelliousness.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:16:2.english: And one does not render forbidden - a woman to her husband because of mere seclusion.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:17:1.english: Shall we say that [it is] not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua - For because of seclusion, he presumes her [to be] one who has had intercourse.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:17:2.english: With regard to lineage - [Meaning,] with regard to the priesthood.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:1:1.hebrew: דא"כ - דרב נחמן לא מיתוקם כרבן גמליאל אלא כרבי יהושע, קשיא הלכתא אהלכתא:
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:1:1.english: For if so - [meaning] that Rav Nachman is not established [as ruling] like Rabban Gamliel, but rather like Rabbi Yehoshua, [then] one halakha contradicts another halakha.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:2:1.english: You are trampled by a man - Before I betrothed you.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:3:1.english: What are their claims - What is she claiming from him, and what does he want to give?

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:3:2.hebrew: במאתים ומנה - היא אומרת: מוכת עץ אני ויש לי מאתים, ואע"פ שלא הכרת בי. והוא אומר: דרוסת איש את ואין לך אלא מנה. וקסבר: כנסה בחזקת בתולה ונמצאת בעולה — יש לה כתובה מנה:
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:3:2.english: Over two hundred and a maneh - She says: "I was injured by wood, so I am entitled to two hundred [dinars], even though you did not recognize [it] in me." And he says: "You had intercourse with a man, so you are entitled to only a maneh [one hundred dinars]." And [Rabbi Yoḥanan] holds [that if] one married a woman with the presumption [that she was] a virgin and she was found to have had intercourse, she has a ketubah of a maneh.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:3:3.hebrew: במנה ולא כלום - היא תובעת מנה, והוא אומר: אין ליך כלום:
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:3:3.english: Concerning a maneh or nothing - She claims a maneh [one hundred dinars], and he says, "You have nothing."

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:4:1.hebrew: סבר לה - תנא דמתני', דאילו רבי יוחנן לא שביק רבנן ועביד כר"מ:
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:4:1.english: He holds - [This refers to] the Tanna of the Mishnah, whereas Rabbi Yochanan [himself] would not abandon the Rabbis and act in accordance with Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:6:1.hebrew: קסבר - ר' יוחנן: כנסה בחזקת בתולה ונמצאת בעולה, יש לה מנה. הלכך, על כרחך מוכת עץ דמתני' ר"מ היא, דאמר מאתים, והוא אומר דרוסת איש את ויש ליך מנה. דאי רבנן היא, לא תבעה אלא מנה, והוא אומר דרוסת איש את ויש לך מנה — מאי איכא בין טענתא דידיה לטענתא דידה:
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:6:1.english: He holds - Rabbi Yochanan [holds that if a man] married a woman with the presumptive status of a virgin and she was found [to be] a non-virgin, she is entitled to one hundred [dinars]. Therefore, perforce, [the case of] one whose hymen was ruptured by wood in the Mishnah is [according to] Rabbi Meir, who says [she is entitled to] two hundred [dinars], while he says, "You had intercourse with a man, and you are entitled to one hundred [dinars]." For if it is [according to] the Rabbis, she claims only one hundred [dinars], and he says, "You had intercourse with a man, and you are entitled to one hundred [dinars]" — what [difference] is there between his claim and her claim?

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:7:1.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Elazar - Who says [that a woman who] engaged in intercourse with a man has nothing.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:7:2.hebrew: היינו דקתני תרתי - בבי במתני' גבי פלוגתא דממונא: היא אומרת "משארסתני נאנסתי", והיא אומרת "מוכת עץ אני":
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:7:2.english: That is [why] it teaches two - clauses in the Mishnah regarding a monetary dispute: [one where] she says, "After you betrothed me, I was raped," and [one where] she says, "I am injured by wood."

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:7:3.hebrew: חדא לאפוקי מדרמי בר חמא וחדא לאפוקי כו' - "היא אומרת משארסתני נאנסתי", תנא למיתני בה "והיה מקחי מקח טעות" — לגמרי משמע, ואין לה כלום — לאפוקי מדרב חייא בר אבין, דאמר לעיל (כתובות דף יא:): "כנסה בחזקת בתולה ונמצאת בעולה, יש לה כתובה מנה". ותנא "היא אומרת מוכת עץ אני", לאפוקי מדרמי בר חמא, דאמר לעיל גבי מוכת עץ: "אבל לא הכיר בה, דברי הכל ולא כלום":
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:7:3.english: One to exclude [the opinion] of Rami bar Ḥama, and one to exclude, etc. - [Regarding the mishna beginning] "She says: After you betrothed me, I was violated," [the tanna] taught it in order to state in it [the husband's claim,] "and my acquisition was a mistaken transaction" — [which] implies completely [a mistaken transaction], and she receives nothing — to exclude [the opinion] of Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin, who said above (Ketubot 11b): "If one married a woman on the presumption that she was a virgin and she was found to have had intercourse, she has a marriage contract of one hundred [dinars]." And [the tanna] taught [the mishna beginning] "She says: My hymen was ruptured by wood," to exclude [the opinion] of Rami bar Ḥama, who said above regarding [a woman whose hymen was] ruptured by wood: "But if he was not aware of her [condition], everyone agrees [she receives] nothing at all."

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:8:1.hebrew: אלא לרבי יוחנן - דאמר כנסה בחזקת בתולה ונמצאת בעולה, יש לה כתובה מנה. אם כן, מאי מקח טעות דקתני? אמאתים, אבל מנה יש לה. למה לי למיתני כלל לההיא? אי לאשמועינן פלוגתא דרבן גמליאל ור' יהושע בברי ושמא ואוקי ממונא בחזקת מריה, ליתני חדא לאפוקי מדרמי בר חמא ולאשמעינן פלוגתייהו:
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:8:1.english: However, according to Rabbi Yochanan - who says [that if] he married her with the presumptive status of a virgin and she was found to be a non-virgin, she has a ketubah of a maneh [one hundred dinars]: if so, what is [the meaning of] "a mistaken transaction" that [the Mishnah] teaches? [It refers] to [the] two hundred [dinars], but a maneh she does have. Why do I need [the Tanna] to teach that [first Mishnah] at all? If [it was] to teach us the dispute of Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua regarding "certain" versus "uncertain" and "leave money in the possession of its owner," let [the Tanna] teach [just] one [Mishnah] to exclude [the view of] Rami bar Chama and to teach us their dispute.

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:9:1.english: That there is [room] to say a miggo - Since if she wanted, she could have said, "I am injured by wood [mukat etz]."

Rashi on Ketubot 13a:9:2.hebrew: בתרייתא - ליכא למימר מגו לר' יוחנן, דמוקי מתני' כרבי מאיר, דאמר מוכת עץ שלא הכיר בה כתובתה מאתים. ליכא שום מגו, דמה לי אומרת מוכת עץ אני תחתיך, מה לי אמרה מעיקרא:
Rashi on Ketubot 13a:9:2.english: The second [mishna] - There is no [room] to say miggo according to Rabbi Yochanan, who establishes the Mishna in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who says [that for] a mukat eitz [a woman whose hymen was ruptured by wood] whom [her husband] did not recognize [as such], her ketubah is two hundred [zuz]. There is no miggo at all, for what is the difference to me [whether] she says, "I am a mukat eitz [injured] under you," [or] what is the difference to me [whether] she said [it happened] from the outset.

Tosafot on Ketubot 13a:12:1.hebrew: רב אסי אמר נבעלה - אבל נסתרה, מודה ר' יהושע דנאמנת לומר "לכשר נבעלתי", במגו דאי בעיא אמרה "לא נבעלתי". וא"ת: והא רבי יהושע לית ליה מגו גבי "משארסתני נאנסתי"? ויש לומר: דהתם לא הוי מגו גמור, דהא אפילו אמרה "מוכת עץ אני" אינה נאמנת לרבי יהושע, כדתנן במתני'; ולא קרי ליה מגו אלא לפי שהיא טענה מעולה ביותר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 13a:12:1.english: Rav Asi said: She engaged in intercourse - However, [if she merely] secluded herself, Rabbi Yehoshua concedes that she is believed to say, "I engaged in intercourse with a fit [man]," by virtue of a migo, [since] if she wanted, she could have said, "I did not engage in intercourse." And if you ask: But Rabbi Yehoshua does not accept a migo regarding [the case of] "After you betrothed me, I was raped"? One can say that there it is not a complete migo, for even if she says, "I am mukkat etz [injured by a piece of wood]," she is not believed according to Rabbi Yehoshua, as we learned in the Mishnah; and it is only called a migo because it is a superior claim.

Tosafot on Ketubot 13a:14:1.hebrew: חדא להכשיר בה וחדא להכשיר בבתה - וצריכי תרוייהו: חדא להודיעך כחו דרבן גמליאל, וחדא להודיעך כחו דרבי יהושע:
Tosafot on Ketubot 13a:14:1.english: "One [case] to deem her fit, and one [case] to deem her daughter fit" - And both are necessary: one to inform you of the strength of Rabban Gamliel's [position], and one to inform you of the strength of Rabbi Yehoshua's [position].

Tosafot on Ketubot 13a:15:1.english: According to the statement of the one who deems her fit, he deems her daughter unfit - And [the reason the Mishnah] mentioned "pregnant" [is] because of a euphemistic expression:

Tosafot on Ketubot 13a:16:1.hebrew: ואין אוסרין על היחוד לימא דלא כרבי יהושע - תימה לרשב"א, דלזעירי (נמי) דאמר נסתרה, איירי כגון דמודה היא שנבעלה; דאי אמרה "לא נבעלתי", אם כן הוי ספק ספיקא, דמכשיר רבי יהושע, כדאמר לקמן: "התם ספק ספיקא". ויש לומר דלעולם איירי דקאמרה לא נבעלה, וחשיב ליה חדא ספיקא משום דאין אפוטרופוס לעריות. אבל קשה, דבהדי' משמע בריש פרק שני (לקמן כתובות טז.) דאיירי בנבעלת, דקאמר: "הניחא לזעירי דאמר מאי מדברת נסתרה, דמגו דאי בעיא אמרה לא נבעלתי מהימנא" כו'. לכך נראה דפריך לזעירי: דבספיקא חדא אסרינן לה, והא יחוד דאשת איש דספיקא חדא היא — ואין אוסרים על היחוד. וק"ק, דלכאורה נראה דיחוד איחוד פריך, מדפריך לזעירי ולא לרב אסי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 13a:16:1.english: But one does not render [a woman] forbidden for seclusion — shall we say that [this is] not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua? - This is astonishing to Rashba: for according to Ze'eiri (as well), who says [that "speaking" means] "she secluded herself," [the Mishnah] is dealing with a case where she admits that she engaged in intercourse; for if she said, "I did not engage in intercourse," then it would be a double doubt, in which Rabbi Yehoshua declares [her] fit, as [the Gemara] says below, "There it is a double doubt." And one can say that actually [the Mishnah] is dealing with a case where she says she did not engage in intercourse, yet [Rabbi Yehoshua] considers it a single doubt because "there is no guardian against forbidden sexual relations." However, [this is] difficult, for it is explicitly implied at the beginning of the second chapter (below, Ketubot 16a) that [the Mishnah] is dealing with [a woman] who engaged in intercourse, as [the Gemara] says: "This works out well according to Ze'eiri, who said: What is [the meaning of] 'speaking'? She secluded herself — for since if she wanted she could have said, 'I did not engage in intercourse,' she is deemed credible, etc." Therefore, it appears that [Rav Pappa] is asking against Ze'eiri [as follows]: that on a single doubt we forbid her [to the priesthood], yet behold, the seclusion of a married woman is a single doubt, and [yet] one does not render [her] forbidden [to her husband] for seclusion. And it is somewhat difficult, for seemingly it appears that he is asking from seclusion upon seclusion, since he asks against Ze'eiri and not against Rav Assi.

Tosafot on Ketubot 13a:17:1.hebrew: מעלה עשו ביוחסין - תימה, דמשמע דאין אוסרין על היחוד איירי באשת איש ולא בפנויה; ובסוף קדושין (דף פא. ושם) מוקי מלקין על היחוד דוקא בפנויה, אבל באשת איש לא, דאתה מוציא לעז על בניה. ואפי' למר זוטרא דמלקין ומכריז באשת איש, מודה דבפנויה נמי איירי. ואור"ת, דאף על גב דמלקין על היחוד איירי בפנויה, אין אוסרין על היחוד לא איירי אלא באשת איש. וא"ת: והא אמרינן בפ' בתרא דנדרים (דף צא:) גבי ההוא נואף דעייל לגבה דההיא איתתא — אמר ליה נואף: "לא תיכול מינהון, דטעמינהו חויא", אמר רבא: "איתתא שריא; אם איתא דעבד איסורא, ניחא ליה דלימות" — משמע דאי לאו האי טעמא היתה נאסרת על ידי יחוד? ויש לומר דנואף שאני. וה"ר יוסף דשליטן תירץ, דאין אוסרים על היחוד איירי בפנויה כמו מלקין על היחוד, ולא איירי לכהונה, אלא אין אוסרין אותה לבנו כשתתייחד עם אביו, לרבי יהודה דאסר באנוסת אביו (יבמות דף צז.):
Tosafot on Ketubot 13a:17:1.english: "They established a higher standard with regard to lineage" - This is surprising, for it implies that [the statement] "they do not forbid [her] on account of seclusion" refers to a married woman and not to an unmarried woman; yet at the end of Kiddushin (81a and there), [the Gemara] establishes [that] "they administer lashes for seclusion" [applies] specifically to an unmarried woman, but not to a married woman, because [otherwise] you cast aspersion upon her children. And even according to Mar Zutra, who [holds that] they administer lashes and make a proclamation in the case of a married woman, he concedes that it also refers to an unmarried woman. And Rabbeinu Tam says that even though "they administer lashes for seclusion" refers to an unmarried woman, "they do not forbid [her] on account of seclusion" refers only to a married woman. And if you will say: Behold, we say in the last chapter of Nedarim (91b) regarding that adulterer who entered to [be with] a certain [married] woman — the adulterer said to [her husband]: "Do not eat from them, for a snake tasted them," [and] Rava said: "The woman is permitted [to her husband]; if it were so that he committed a sin [with her], it would be preferable to him that [the husband] die" — [which] implies that were it not for this reason, she would be forbidden [to her husband] on account of seclusion? And one can say that [the case of] an adulterer is different. And Rabbi Yosef of Shlitan answered that "they do not forbid [her] on account of seclusion" refers to an unmarried woman, just like "they administer lashes for seclusion," and it does not refer to [marrying into] the priesthood; rather, they do not forbid her to his son when she secludes herself with his father, according to Rabbi Yehudah who forbids a woman violated by one's father (Yevamot 97a).
